key_insight: MATTRL enables multi-agent LLM collaborators to adapt and improve reasoning at test time by injecting structured textual experience into their deliberation loop—avoiding costly, unstable multi-agent RL training while retaining cross-checking benefits.
problem_solved: Addresses the resource intensity, instability, and sparse/noisy reward challenges of conventional multi-agent RL by enabling on-the-fly policy improvement using textual experiences during inference rather than full MARL training.
method: Run diverse LLM agents in a deliberation loop where proposals, critiques, and outcomes are captured as structured textual experience.
Apply lightweight test-time RL updates (reward signals derived from textual feedback, preference or credit-assignment heuristics) to bias subsequent agent selection and responses.
Leverage cross-checking and ensemble diversity to stabilize learning and reduce dependence on long, expensive co-training of agents.
impact: Practitioners can get robust, adaptive multi-agent reasoning without expensive MARL pipelines—improving correctness and reliability of LLM collaborations in downstream tasks with lower compute and more stable behavior.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: LLM agents → deliberation (propose/critique) → structured textual experience → test-time RL update → improved responses
Before/After chart: performance or error rate with standard MARL vs MATTRL at test time
Icon grid: agents (multiple LLMs), textual experience (document icon), reward signal (star/score), and iteration loop
Sequence example: short annotated dialogue showing how a critique becomes a reward signal and changes the next reply
paper_title: Collaborative Multi-Agent Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning
paper_authors: Zhiyuan Hu, Yunhai Hu, Juncheng Liu, Shuyue Stella Li, Yucheng Wang
